scope: Read-only bounded reported st_blocks survey of one exact marked private sync workspace
status: independently reviewed; scoped native gates passed
findings_fixed: Darwin filesystem ID alone conflated equal-Fsid/different-reported-mountpoint identities; require Fsid and nonempty descriptor Mntonname
Symlink inodes skipped mount checks despite Linux supporting a mounted symlink itself; check every permitted inode kind before and after traversal
The first Darwin O_SYMLINK plus O_NOFOLLOW combination refused ordinary symlink surveys; use native O_SYMLINK semantics and prove the descriptor is the original link inode
reviewed_native_mechanics: Original reservation and held selected/parent/base/stage/quarantine identity inspected before observation
Linux requires reported STATX_MNT_ID without a device-only fallback
Darwin uses descriptor Fsid plus nonempty reported mountpoint; no Linux-equivalence claim
Directories opened relative to held descriptors with no-follow and before/after object/block/link checks
Reported hardlinks count per directory entry, sparse files use reported blocks, symlink payload targets are excluded
Entry ceiling100000 and depth ceiling128; negative/overflow block reports and failures return no usable partial Survey result

native_linux.default_skip: The explicitly gated mount fixture skips in ordinary package execution, then executes successfully as a separate guarded native root with directory/file/symlink cases. No unchecked mount gate remains.

private_mount_proof.snapshot_access_time_exception: Access time is excluded because native reads may update it; names, ownership, modes, device/inode, sizes, links, blocks, modification/change times and payload/link target evidence are compared

native_darwin.actual_symlink_descriptor: Fstat reports original S_IFLNK/same inode and Fstatfs reports its containing mount, without following target
native_darwin.mount_counterexample_limit: Equal-Fsid/different-Mntonname and empty-Mntonname are pure Statfs value tests; no actual Darwin bind mount counterexample executed

earlier_evidence_preserved.scope: Earlier source passed both OSes, including actual Linux file/directory bind negatives; not used as acceptance for later symlink changes
Two actual ordinary-symlink survey refusals on earlier Darwin flag combination retained; Linux native successor passed

limits: No reservation, write cap, kernel quota, measured exclusive allocation or peak-space enforcement added
st_blocks may double count hardlinks, clones and shared blocks; it does not prove physical reclamation
No cleanup, promise release, lease settlement, worker dispatch, public sync or route authority added
No atomic snapshot against concurrent same-account writers; cancellation is checked between native cuts and cannot force stalled kernel I/O to return
Native scope is hosted Linux amd64 and macOS arm64; no new Linux ARM64 or real Darwin mount-negative evidence
Broader public sync allocation/dispatch and formal conformance remain required
